newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico stocks seen mixed, market awaiting FOMC.
newsitem.headline: Mexico stocks seen mixed, market awaiting FOMC.

text.p: --Mexico stocks may edge up but cautious trade seen
--Peso likely stable on U.S. long bond
--Cetes overnight rate viewed higher on profit-taking
Dealers saw Mexican stocks opening mixed with an upside bias on Tuesday amid cautious trade watching moves on Wall Street and awaiting the early afternoon U.S. Federal Open Market Committee decision.
"We have some buy orders left over but see little action until the Fed announces a decision," a desk trader said.
Technical analysts placed resistance at 4,970 points on the IPC scale, up from Monday's close of 4,952.88.
Foreign exchange traders expected the peso to open stable on small changes in U.S. long bond yields, and said they saw the peso firming slightly if the FOMC did not revise U.S. interest rates.
Dealers forecast a trading range of 7.7600/7.7700 per dollar for the 48-hour peso. Pre-open bids stood at 7.7575/7.7670 per dollar, compared to Monday's close of 7.7730/7.7760.
Overnight rates on Cetes were seen opening up on profit-taking after Monday's low close of 17.30 percent.
